domains.name: COST OF CAPITAL CONCEPTS AND METHODOLOGY, AND OTHER PRICING MODELS

domain_guidance.summary: This domain carefully covers overview principles and introductory framework concepts that are fundamentally required for valuation analysts entering the profession and beginning their practice within the financial industry environment successfully.

This specific domain focuses heavily on professional responsibilities, strict ethics, and various regulatory standards governing valuation practitioners throughout all phases of their daily business engagements and reporting duties as outlined by the organization.

This domain carefully addresses engagement acceptance procedures, detailed scoping requirements, and effective planning processes necessary for managing client projects successfully from initial initiation through final delivery of reports.

This domain deals with qualitative analysis techniques used to accurately assess business history, competitive industry environments, and broader economic outlook conditions impacting subject companies during all stages of valuations.

This domain strongly emphasizes quantitative analysis methods, complex financial statement adjustments, and earning capacity evaluations vital for reliable business valuation determinations across diverse operational environments and business structures.

This domain covers asset-based, market, and income valuation approaches and analytical methods which constitute the largest weighted portion of the entire certification examination content for all participating candidates.

This domain explores complex cost of capital concepts, computational methodologies, and alternative pricing models required to determine appropriate discount rates for business valuation assignments and financial calculations accurately.

This specific domain examines discounts, premiums, and other necessary adjustments for non-controlling ownership interests and lack of marketability within private company valuation reports prepared for various financial advisory clients.

This domain addresses unique special purpose valuation topics and alternative applications that fall outside standard ongoing business valuation operating engagements and standard reporting formats currently utilized by practitioners.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Manage your testing time effectively across the 400 total questions during the strictly enforced 300 minutes allotted for the official certification examination session to ensure success.

faq.answer_text: The certification examination consists of exactly 400 questions covering nine different domains of valuation knowledge, professional standards, and analytical techniques required by NACVA for candidates.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: Candidates are given a total duration of 300 minutes to complete all questions within the official testing environment provided for the credential program administration by the organization.

The credential and its associated certification examination are administered directly and exclusively by NACVA, known formally as the National Association of Certified Valuators and Analysts organization.
This certification path is active and current; please check with NACVA for any official updates regarding testing requirements and candidate handbook revisions before applying for the credential.

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the CVA Certified Valuation Analyst exam from NACVA, featuring 400 questions and a duration of 300 minutes for candidates.

methodology.summary: This page was built using official NACVA exam guide data and professional standards documentation to outline domain weights, structural requirements, question totals, and examination duration parameters accurately.

editorial.overview: The CVA Certified Valuation Analyst credential is administered by NACVA and evaluates knowledge across nine specific domains, featuring a total of 400 questions to be completed during 300 minutes. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in valuation approaches, professional responsibilities, fundamental analysis, and business valuation concepts required for financial analysts seeking formal recognition through this credential program.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review NACVA professional standards and candidate handbooks carefully while establishing a disciplined and thorough study routine over many weeks of preparation. Focus extensive preparation time on quantitative analysis, valuation approaches, and cost of capital concepts, because these specific subject sections represent large percentage weights on the official certification examination.
editorial.who_should_take: Financial analysts, accountants, and valuation professionals seeking official certification from NACVA to establish recognized expertise in business valuation engagements, methodologies, industry standards, and professional practices.

lifecycle.summary: Confirmed current on the issuer host on 2026-09-19: "Exam Fee: $625 each, for either the Certified Valuation Analyst® (CVA®) or Master Analyst in Financial Forensics® (MAFF®) credential exam."
